facts.text: Weir, Mississippi was founded in 1870 by Confederate Colonel John Weir, who built a water‑powered sawmill and gristmill that gave the town its name.
The Yockanookany River borders Weir to the north, a tributary of the Pearl River that has shaped local flooding patterns.
Weir’s early mills powered cotton agriculture, anchoring the town’s growth amid southwestern Choctaw County’s late‑19th‑century cotton boom.
Weir incorporated on February 16, 1884, formalizing its status as a municipality after years of informal settlement.
A violent tornado struck Weir on April 24, 2010, causing significant damage and leaving a lasting memory among residents.
The John Weir House, recognized by a state historical marker in 2013, stands as a tangible reminder of the town’s founding era.
